title: AccessDoc evidence receipt, schema 1.2
description: Machine-readable contract for receipt.json inside an AccessDoc evidence bundle. Schema 1.2 adds per-finding identity: rule_ids, violations[] with normalized targets, and a finding_fingerprint derived from the canonical {rule, source, target} triple. A receipt validating against this schema is STRUCTURALLY valid; it is not thereby authentic. Authenticity requires re-deriving every finding_fingerprint (app/receipt_validate.py), verifying the bundle manifest digests, and verifying the Sigstore signature over the bundle. Audit dates are caller-supplied and are NOT independently timestamped.

schema_version.description: Receipt schema version. 1.0 and 1.1 receipts remain readable by verifiers but carry strictly less identity: 1.1 has rule-level identity only, 1.0 is aggregate-only.

accessdoc_version.description: Version of the generator that produced this receipt.

axe_core_verified_version.description: axe-core version this build's WCAG mapping catalog was verified against.

catalog_version.description: Version of the internal rule to WCAG success-criteria mapping catalog.

coverage_note.description: Mandatory honesty statement. Automated scanning detects roughly 30-57% of WCAG issues; absence of findings is never evidence of conformance.

audit_date.description: Caller-supplied audit date. NOT a trusted timestamp.

rule_ids.description: Sorted set of rule ids present in violations[]. Must agree exactly with the ids in violations[].

finding_fingerprint_version.description: Fingerprint derivation version. Version 1 = SHA-256 over the canonical JSON encoding of {"rule", "source", "target"} with sorted keys, no whitespace, ensure_ascii=false, UTF-8 encoded. A verifier that does not recognise this version MUST degrade to rule-level comparison rather than guess.

source.description: Origin of the finding, e.g. axe or manual.

target.description: Normalized element identity: the axe target selector chain joined with ' > ', control characters stripped, bounded to 200 characters. When no usable target exists the deterministic fallback '<rule-id>:no-target' is used, which yields rule-level identity only for that finding.

finding_fingerprint.description: Lowercase SHA-256 hex digest, never truncated. MUST re-derive from this finding's own {rule, source, target}.
